purpose: Candidate domain models driven by user decisions. This hierarchy is navigation, not inheritance or a list of approved C# records.
ratingBasis: Editorial hypotheses based on the current user/workflow catalog and synthetic acceptance stories. No usage-frequency study or source-feasibility verification has been performed.

domains.name: Identity and source history
domains.meaning: A real/logical thing is distinct from the source rows and representations describing it

models.name: Source revision changes
models.question: Which scope changed between issued models?
models.grain: One proposed object change between two snapshots
models.separateBecause: Change review needs before-and-after meaning beyond source row identifiers
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer until correspondence is defensible; uncertain matches remain candidates

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Change review needs before-and-after meaning beyond source row identifiers

priority.rationale: Useful at new-delivery comparisons. The user describes data as infrequently updated, so revision comparison should not outrank every recurring query by an assumed frequent-change cadence.

domains.name: Project and place
domains.meaning: Recognizable locations; overlapping zones and multi-storey objects remain possible

models.name: Space
models.question: Which spaces exist and what activities and services belong to them?
models.grain: One bounded or explicitly scheduled space occurrence
models.separateBecause: Room identity and room fields support many tasks
models.mergeOrDefer: Treat room as a space use; avoid classes per room function

existingContract.incrementalGain: A typed space view would add room number, use, measured area and enclosure meaning over shared object identity; it must not create another identity.

scenarioSupport.supports: Stable room references let opposite wall faces carry separate finish quantities.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Space enclosure, occupancy and room-area definitions.

priority.rationale: Room-facing finishes and service traces need stable space references; area and enclosure require separate evidence.
priority.whyNow: Provides a recognizable shared context for architectural schedules, finishes, services and handover without classes for each room use.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can we give a room-based work list when some spaces are only scheduled, their enclosure is unknown, and services or finishes have no resolved room?

models.name: Storey
models.question: What belongs to this building level and what does its elevation mean?
models.decision: Navigate and group work by level
models.grain: One named building level
models.separateBecause: A common grouping dimension needs elevation semantics
models.mergeOrDefer: Use associations for multi-level objects; distinguish finish and structural levels

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; A common grouping dimension needs elevation semantics

priority.rationale: Expected frequent grouping value; existing workflows do not yet settle alternative level conventions.

models.name: Functional zone membership
models.question: Which spaces form this department or service zone?
models.grain: One object membership in a named zone under a purpose
models.separateBecause: Departments and service areas overlap beyond a place hierarchy
models.mergeOrDefer: Use controlled purposes; specialize only when rules differ

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Departments and service areas overlap beyond a place hierarchy

priority.rationale: May remove repeated manual grouping; regulated safety zones require stronger rules than generic membership.

domains.name: Coordinates and representations
domains.meaning: Position/orientation, parent frames, 2D/3D shape and selectable detail

models.name: Service access envelope
models.question: Can someone operate or remove this component in the required direction?
models.grain: One required envelope for an object and operation
models.separateBecause: Operational clearance differs from physical shape
models.mergeOrDefer: Start from supplied requirements; do not infer safe clearance from generic dimensions

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Operational clearance differs from physical shape

priority.rationale: Blocked panels and inaccessible valves cause rework; models may lack the clearance shape and its authority.

models.name: Spatial conflict candidates
models.question: Which objects might intersect this work area or clearance?
models.decision: Narrow precise geometry and human review
models.grain: One candidate pair or object-region hit for a named test
models.separateBecause: Screening is an operation producing bounded results
models.mergeOrDefer: Use bounds first and exact geometry selectively

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Screening is an operation producing bounded results

priority.rationale: Expected broad coordination value at scale; approximate overlap must never become a confirmed clash.

domains.name: Building fabric
domains.meaning: Common components with useful typed fields and spatial/contextual links

models.name: Door
models.question: Does this door configuration meet the intended opening function?
models.grain: One door occurrence with explicit leaf or assembly scope
models.separateBecause: Operation and clear opening recur in practical tasks
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep hardware linked; settle leaf versus assembly counting

existingContract.incrementalGain: Extend existing door audit projection with scope/operation/space concepts only where a new question requires them.

scenarioSupport.supports: Missing width/rating evidence prevents a complete audit.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Door operation, leaf-versus-assembly rules and connected-space topology.

priority.rationale: The current door_schedule already answers the worked width/rating audit. Additional value concerns operation, opening scope and space relationships; these need new examples.

models.name: Window
models.question: Which glazed openings share size and performance requirements?
models.decision: Package glazing and review envelope inputs
models.grain: One window unit at an explicit unit or assembly scope
models.separateBecause: Glazed openings have recurring dimensions and performance fields
models.mergeOrDefer: Use roles for operability; evaluate curtain-wall panel grain separately

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Glazed openings have recurring dimensions and performance fields

priority.rationale: Expected glazing schedule value; current envelope workflow provides only a broad requirement.

models.name: Stair
models.question: Which levels does this stair connect and what route dimensions are known?
models.grain: One stair assembly with optional flight detail
models.separateBecause: A level connection is useful before every tread is modeled
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer flight and landing records until an assessment needs their separate geometry

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; A level connection is useful before every tread is modeled

priority.rationale: Recognizable circulation data helps review; a simple stair record cannot establish compliant egress.

models.name: Wall
models.question: Which walls separate this area and what construction is intended?
models.grain: One wall occurrence with identifiable faces and assembly
models.separateBecause: Host identity connects construction to separate room-facing surfaces
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep finishes on surfaces; do not assign one universal room to a wall

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Host identity connects construction to separate room-facing surfaces

scenarioSupport.supports: One physical wall can have two separately measured finishes.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Wall construction layers, loadbearing role and complete opening deductions.

priority.rationale: The finish scenario proves two faces of one wall must remain distinct; broader wall fields need validation.

models.name: Floor construction
models.question: Which floor construction and finishes are in scope?
models.grain: One floor construction occurrence at a declared scope
models.separateBecause: Construction and finish installation have different quantities and ownership
models.mergeOrDefer: Use a structural-role facet rather than duplicate slab identity

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Construction and finish installation have different quantities and ownership

priority.rationale: May reduce slab-versus-finish double counting; the flooring workflow has not settled construction boundaries.

models.name: Roof
models.question: How much roof surface needs each assembly and what remains unknown?
models.decision: Prepare takeoff with the correct basis
models.grain: One roof occurrence or explicitly partitioned construction scope
models.separateBecause: Surface and projected areas need distinct names
models.mergeOrDefer: Use assembly layers rather than classes per roofing product

existingContract.incrementalGain: Extend assembly or edge details after testing the gap; reuse existing area selection and occurrence identity.

scenarioSupport.supports: Net surface, projected area, competing observations and unmeasured scope differ.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Layer ordering, roof drainage and edge details.

priority.rationale: The current roof_takeoff already separates net and projected areas. Construction/edge detail is an extension, not a reason to duplicate roof identity or selected measurements.

models.name: Service penetration
models.question: Which openings need approval and a compatible firestop detail?
models.grain: One opening through a host with linked passing services
models.separateBecause: Openings span trades and have independent approval work
models.mergeOrDefer: Link firestop specifications; do not infer required ratings from host names

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add the host-opening/passing-service/approval association and distinguish required from observed firestop evidence.

priority.rationale: Expected rework and safety value; current coordination cases do not yet validate a penetration approval workflow.
priority.whyNow: Adds a cross-trade coordination case beyond familiar component schedules: a host opening, several passing services and independent approval/firestop evidence. Doors already have a bounded audit projection to refine later.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can the contractor identify which service penetrations need approval or firestop evidence before closing a wall, without inferring ratings or approvals from object names?

domains.name: Structure and civil
domains.meaning: Structural and site objects; linear and surface features as well as solids

models.name: Structural member
models.question: Which members share section and material and measurable lengths?
models.grain: One physical structural member at an explicit occurrence scope
models.separateBecause: Beams columns and braces share section and axis data
models.mergeOrDefer: Use member roles; do not treat physical geometry as an analysis model

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add typed section/material/axis relationships for physical member schedules; reuse object identity and quantity evidence.

priority.rationale: Expected steel and timber schedule value; connection and analysis detail should follow proven needs.
priority.whyNow: Adds structural trade requirements early and tests where beams, columns and braces can share stable fields without importing an analytical structural hierarchy.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can a fabricator group members by section and material and use measured lengths without substituting bounding-box dimensions or counting analytical duplicates?

models.name: Reinforcement fabrication takeoff
models.question: Which bar shapes and counts are ready for fabrication by pour?
models.grain: One selected bar mark and shape within a fabrication scope
models.separateBecause: Fabrication requires more readiness than concrete quantities
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer until bar shapes and regional scheduling rules exist; do not infer bars from concrete geometry

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Fabrication requires more readiness than concrete quantities

priority.rationale: Potential reinforcement-trade value but detailed source coverage and fabrication rules make this a poor early default.

models.name: Foundation
models.question: Which foundations need concrete and excavation scope at what elevation?
models.grain: One footing pile or foundation assembly at explicit countable scope
models.separateBecause: Bearing and ground context exceed generic member length
models.mergeOrDefer: Use roles for piles and caps until separate fields are justified

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Bearing and ground context exceed generic member length

priority.rationale: Expected quantity value; foundation volume and excavation volume cannot be treated as equivalent.

models.name: Earthwork zone
models.question: Where do existing and proposed ground imply cut or fill?
models.grain: One named earthwork scope with existing and proposed surfaces
models.separateBecause: Earthworks need two surface states rather than one object volume
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer computed volumes until surface coverage and datum alignment are established

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Earthworks need two surface states rather than one object volume

priority.rationale: Expected civil value; the broad landscape workflow does not yet justify an earthworks calculation engine.

domains.name: Interiors and landscape
domains.meaning: Surfaces and assemblies that trades measure and specify

models.name: Finish surface
models.question: Which face needs which finish and how much net area?
models.decision: Order materials and assign finish work
models.grain: One distinct finish-bearing surface partition with optional space association
models.separateBecause: The measured and specified unit is a face rather than its host
models.mergeOrDefer: Allow unassigned spaces and surface partitions; tag paint tile and coverings

existingContract.incrementalGain: Test whether the existing face record can serve the domain after clearer naming; add partition/specification detail only if required.

scenarioSupport.supports: Face identity prevents host-based finish double counting.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: All finish partition rules or product specifications.

priority.rationale: finish_schedule already represents distinct faces and unresolved spaces. Review its domain naming and surface partitions before adding another record with the same grain.
priority.whyNow: A worked shared-wall example already exposes the correct measurement grain. Start from finish_schedule and test whether it can serve the domain directly before creating another record.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can painters, flooring and ceiling trades share a finish-face model that preserves partitions, unknown areas and unassigned spaces without counting the host twice?

models.name: Ceiling
models.question: Which ceiling construction and elevation applies and where is access required?
models.grain: One ceiling construction occurrence with associated spaces and surfaces
models.separateBecause: Ceiling datum and access differ from floor surface information
models.mergeOrDefer: Use shared assemblies and surfaces; defer grid and hanger detail until needed

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Ceiling datum and access differ from floor surface information

priority.rationale: Expected reflected-ceiling coordination value; current workflows have not established tile-level requirements.

models.name: Room fitout schedule
models.question: What finishes fixtures and equipment are specified per room and what is missing?
models.grain: One room and fitout category with linked selected items
models.separateBecause: Room review combines records without duplicating their identities
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep a view; expected categories come from project requirements

existingContract.incrementalGain: Compose room-based procurement/context without a second identity or finish measurement store.

priority.rationale: Combines existing finish and asset concepts into a useful room view. Its incremental benefit is coordination and packaging, not a new physical-object identity.

models.name: Planting area
models.question: Which areas need which planting and soil preparation quantities?
models.grain: One bounded planting or soil-preparation area at a declared layer scope
models.separateBecause: Area-based planting differs from individually tracked assets
models.mergeOrDefer: Separate area and soil-layer quantities; avoid classes per species

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Area-based planting differs from individually tracked assets

priority.rationale: Expected landscape-trade value; ecological outcomes require more than planting area and species labels.

models.name: Landscape asset
models.question: Which individual trees or furnishings need installation or care records?
models.decision: Count and hand over selected assets
models.grain: One individually tracked landscape occurrence
models.separateBecause: Individual care can require identity beyond a planting polygon
models.mergeOrDefer: Use roles initially; keep bulk planting area-based and defer botanical lifecycle detail

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Individual care can require identity beyond a planting polygon

priority.rationale: Useful when individual tracking is required; low-value identities for every planting would inflate the model.

domains.name: Systems and equipment
domains.meaning: Connectivity, membership, flow/medium and service relationships are distinct

models.name: Equipment and plant overview
models.question: Which plant items exist by system and what handover or connection data is missing?
models.decision: Navigate equipment and review common handover coverage
models.grain: One identified equipment occurrence in a cross-system overview
models.separateBecause: A cross-system overview helps navigation without defining every machine through generic properties
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep this a view; pump duty and air-handler performance need separate typed records when specific workflows justify them

existingContract.incrementalGain: Compose inventory and handover coverage from existing concepts; specialized equipment fields belong in concrete models or justified facets.

scenarioSupport.supports: A maintainable asset stays visible despite missing handover data.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Pump/head curves, air-handler duties or generic equipment performance fields.

priority.rationale: component_schedule and asset_register already provide much of the inventory. A cross-system overview adds readable joins and gaps; it does not justify a generic duty model.

models.name: Air terminal
models.question: Which terminal serves each space at what design airflow?
models.decision: Coordinate terminal schedules and ceiling openings
models.grain: One air terminal occurrence serving a space or zone
models.separateBecause: Room service and airflow exceed generic equipment naming
models.mergeOrDefer: Use roles for diffusers and grilles; distinguish design and measured flow

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Room service and airflow exceed generic equipment naming

priority.rationale: Expected mechanical value; terminal proximity cannot prove connectivity or balanced airflow.

models.name: Sanitary fixture
models.question: Which fixtures are specified per space and what connections are required?
models.decision: Count and coordinate supply and waste scope
models.grain: One installed or scheduled sanitary fixture occurrence
models.separateBecause: Toilets basins and showers share schedule and connection needs
models.mergeOrDefer: Use a toilet role; add a subtype only for repeated distinct fields

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add fixture role and explicit supply/waste and water-use bases, retaining shared physical identity.

priority.rationale: Expected plumbing and interior value; fixture units and consumption require explicit rule or measurement bases.
priority.whyNow: Tests a useful practical family containing toilets and basins, with real connection and water-use differences, instead of one class for every fixture label.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can a plumber produce a per-space fixture and connection schedule without treating missing waste/supply ports as absent services or mixing water-use bases?

models.name: Drain inlet
models.question: Which areas discharge through each drain and what outlet data is known?
models.grain: One drain inlet with declared catchment references
models.separateBecause: A drain links a surface catchment with a network
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep catchments explicit; defer hydraulic inference until boundary conditions exist

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; A drain links a surface catchment with a network

priority.rationale: Expected cross-trade value; the roof scenario covers areas and does not validate drainage logic.

models.name: Fire-protection terminal
models.question: Which heads or service outlets belong to each protection system and lack inspection data?
models.grain: One terminal occurrence with declared protection role
models.separateBecause: Protection roles and inspection needs recur over project stages
models.mergeOrDefer: Use explicit roles; defer coverage and hydraulic adequacy calculations

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Protection roles and inspection needs recur over project stages

priority.rationale: Expected fire-trade schedule value; missing terminals cannot establish absence or adequate coverage.

models.name: Service route geometry and endpoints
models.question: Where does this service segment run and which endpoints have supported links?
models.decision: Reuse routing context across trade-specific schedules
models.grain: One physical service occurrence and its route representation
models.separateBecause: Route and endpoint context is reusable without replacing discipline-specific records
models.mergeOrDefer: Apply alongside duct and pipe records; trays need their own workflow before further specialization

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Route and endpoint context is reusable without replacing discipline-specific records

scenarioSupport.supports: Accepted service edges differ from candidate proximity edges.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Physical segmentation boundaries, duct construction or pipe pressure semantics.

priority.rationale: Trace cases justify shared routing context; duct airflow and pipe service properties belong to concrete trade records rather than a universal service type.

models.name: Valve
models.question: Which valve controls this branch and can staff identify and reach it?
models.grain: One valve occurrence with a control or isolation role
models.separateBecause: Operational role and normal position matter beyond a fitting count
models.mergeOrDefer: Do not infer safe isolation from tags; defer actuator internals

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Operational role and normal position matter beyond a fitting count

priority.rationale: Expected operating value; trustworthy isolation additionally requires complete topology and current state.

models.name: Duct segment
models.question: Which duct sizes constructions and design airflows are assigned to each HVAC route?
models.decision: Prepare duct schedules and coordinate fabrication scope
models.grain: One physical duct segment with declared segment boundaries
models.separateBecause: Section shape lining and airflow are familiar mechanical fields with distinct meanings
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep fittings as linked occurrences when fabrication needs them; do not derive airflow from geometry

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add duct construction, lining, dimensions and airflow vocabulary; geometry and adjacency alone cannot express it.

priority.rationale: Expected mechanical schedule value; generic connectivity scenarios support links but do not establish duct lining or design-flow evidence.
priority.whyNow: Tests a concrete mechanical model and prevents shared routing geometry from turning into a universal pipe/duct/tray record. Compare with the pipe candidate before approving the shared facet.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can a mechanical trade query duct size, construction, lining and airflow separately from geometry and distinguish an unobserved connection from a disconnected route?

models.name: Pipe segment
models.question: Which pipe sizes materials and service requirements apply to each run?
models.decision: Prepare pipe schedules and check service-specific requirements
models.grain: One physical pipe segment with declared segment boundaries
models.separateBecause: Nominal size service medium and slope or pressure requirements differ from duct airflow fields
models.mergeOrDefer: Use optional drainage or pressure facets where applicable; do not force every pipe to have both

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add pipe material, size and conditional slope/pressure context; share geometry without forcing duct semantics.

priority.rationale: Expected plumbing and mechanical value; slope and pressure remain explicitly conditional rather than inferred from generic route geometry.

models.name: Electrical distribution panel
models.question: Which panel supplies each circuit and what capacity and access information is known?
models.decision: Review supply schedules and isolation scope
models.grain: One panel or electrical board occurrence
models.separateBecause: Circuits and supply characteristics justify a recurring electrical model
models.mergeOrDefer: Start circuit detail as relationships; avoid classes per panel style

existingContract.incrementalGain: Add electrical supply and circuit vocabulary absent from generic component/edge rows.

priority.rationale: Expected electrical-specific value; phase and spare-capacity calculations need explicit conventions.
priority.whyNow: Electrical schedules need distinct supply and circuit concepts that the generic component model cannot make discoverable. This deliberately tests a discipline beyond architectural takeoff.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can an electrician inspect panel and circuit assignments while unknown phases, capacity and upstream connections remain explicit?

models.name: Lighting fixture
models.question: Which luminaires belong to each room and circuit and serve emergency lighting?
models.grain: One installed luminaire occurrence
models.separateBecause: Count power and emergency role recur across electrical and interior tasks
models.mergeOrDefer: Reference photometric files; defer illumination simulation

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Count power and emergency role recur across electrical and interior tasks

priority.rationale: Expected schedule value; emergency role alone cannot prove emergency-lighting compliance.

models.name: Service support assembly
models.question: Which supports carry routes and need attachment approval?
models.grain: One support or rack assembly carrying one or more services
models.separateBecause: Supports span structure and services with independent installation scope
models.mergeOrDefer: Begin with explicit supports; defer automatic layout and seismic detailing

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Supports span structure and services with independent installation scope

priority.rationale: Potential coordination value when detail exists; source coverage may make early support taxonomy expensive.

domains.name: Materials and measurement
domains.meaning: Material contributions and quantities with explicit basis and provenance

models.name: Construction assembly specification
models.question: Which layers and specifications define this construction and what remains unspecified?
models.decision: Reuse specifications and allocate material scope
models.grain: One versioned assembly specification with component ordering defined
models.separateBecause: Shared specifications differ from installed occurrences and quantities
models.mergeOrDefer: Avoid universal composition theory; add layers where takeoff or performance needs them

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Shared specifications differ from installed occurrences and quantities

scenarioSupport.supports: A material contribution must be counted once across source representations.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Ordered assembly layers or a general assembly taxonomy.

priority.rationale: Roof grouping and carbon contributions need reusable specifications; layer ordering and measurement remain open.

models.name: Selected quantity takeoff
models.question: What quantity can I sum and which items remain unmeasured?
models.grain: One selected quantity per subject and basis within a scope
models.separateBecause: Users need additive selected quantities rather than competing observations
models.mergeOrDefer: Preserve observations; never sum overlapping assembly and part scope

existingContract.incrementalGain: Expose selected quantities and missing coverage through a view; preserve the original observations.

scenarioSupport.supports: Select a measurement basis and retain unknown scope.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Every trade measurement convention or aggregation denominator.

priority.rationale: Selected quantity observations and scopes already exist. Additional value is a readable coverage-aware view and documented additive grouping.

domains.name: Commercial and delivery
domains.meaning: A work item can concern multiple objects and may have no independent geometry

models.name: Trade work package
models.question: Which objects and activities are in this package and what prevents release?
models.decision: Assign and price explicit work scope
models.grain: One package within a project planning scenario
models.separateBecause: Commercial scope may contain many objects and tasks without geometry
models.mergeOrDefer: Keep scenarios explicit; avoid building a full scheduling system

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing package scope is sufficient for the worked estimate; release/dependency fields remain an incremental design question.

scenarioSupport.supports: An estimate can price known package scope while preserving unpriced scope.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Schedule dependencies, release rules or installation progress.

priority.rationale: work_packages already scopes the estimate example. Dependencies and release readiness should extend that contract once additional cases establish their meaning.

models.name: Procurement requirement
models.question: Which specified items must be ordered and what prevents ordering?
models.decision: Prepare order scope and resolve selections
models.grain: One required purchasable item or specification in a package and scenario
models.separateBecause: Purchased grouping differs from occurrence and installed quantity
models.mergeOrDefer: Separate requirement from order and shipment; supplier terms require external data

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Purchased grouping differs from occurrence and installed quantity

priority.rationale: Expected contractor value; current scenarios do not provide prices lead times or delivery commitments.

models.name: Installation or delivery observation
models.question: What was delivered or installed against requirements and what supports that observation?
models.decision: Accept flag or clarify an item
models.grain: One dated observation of a subject against a declared stage
models.separateBecause: Site observation differs from design intent and interpretation
models.mergeOrDefer: Record observations first; defer capture apps and transaction systems

existingContract.incrementalGain: Independent delivery or installation events need a subject, event scope and evidence grain separate from the modeled occurrence.

priority.rationale: Door audits motivate this extension but current cases concern model evidence; delivery observations need independent field evidence.
priority.whyNow: Adds delivery and field-audit needs to the first wave. It tests the distinction between what a model specifies and what independent evidence says was delivered or installed.
priority.acceptanceQuestion: Can a project manager reconcile specified items with partial deliveries and repeated observations without treating a modeled object as proof of installation?

domains.name: Operations and performance
domains.meaning: Stable assets plus links to operational records and scenario results

models.name: Asset service requirements
models.question: What documentation access and service obligations belong to this item?
models.grain: One asset and versioned service requirement set
models.separateBecause: Maintainability cuts across physical categories without duplicating identity
models.mergeOrDefer: Apply a facet to existing objects; keep events in operational systems

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Maintainability cuts across physical categories without duplicating identity

scenarioSupport.supports: Missing manuals are a handover gap rather than absence of an asset.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Maintenance intervals, access envelopes or service procedures.

priority.rationale: Handover explicitly tracks unknown manuals and maintainability; extra warranty and service fields require validation.

models.name: Maintenance planning view
models.question: Which services are due and what access or shutdown constraints apply?
models.grain: One asset service task in a planning period and schedule version
models.separateBecause: Service planning combines requirements dates and operating constraints
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer due-date computation until history and authoritative intervals are connected

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Service planning combines requirements dates and operating constraints

priority.rationale: Valuable to facilities but static BIM is insufficient; handover does not justify a maintenance management system.

domains.name: Environment and assessment
domains.meaning: Versioned factors/rules and explainable results with incomplete/unknown outcomes

models.name: Material impact breakdown
models.question: What contributes to carbon results and how much scope lacks factors?
models.grain: One additive contribution and factor application in a scenario and life-cycle module
models.separateBecause: Impact needs factor and module context beyond a material label
models.mergeOrDefer: Retain exclusions and uncertainty; defer full ecological impact claims

existingContract.incrementalGain: Use existing impact grain and factor context; test aggregate coverage rather than creating another result fact.

scenarioSupport.supports: Contribution identity and module/factor context constrain an impact line.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Full portfolio aggregation, lifecycle completeness or ecological-impact methods.

priority.rationale: impact_lines already carries additive contribution, factor and module context. Reuse it for breakdowns; independently prove aggregation and coverage additions.

models.name: Requirement assessment results
models.question: Which requirements passed failed or could not be assessed and why?
models.decision: Direct review to failures and missing evidence
models.grain: One subject against one versioned requirement in a scenario
models.separateBecause: A result is an explainable decision rather than a boolean property
models.mergeOrDefer: Use domain evaluators later; avoid a universal executable rule language now

existingContract.incrementalGain: The existing assessment record already has the requested grain and incomplete outcomes.

scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: Any regulatory rule implementation or complete compliance claim.

priority.rationale: assessments already represents this row grain, result and incomplete inputs. Reuse its result view; a second independent assessment record adds little. This does not devalue safety work.

models.name: Detailed acoustic response
models.question: How might finishes and transmission paths affect room acoustics across frequency bands?
models.grain: One analysis metric for a space or path and frequency band in a scenario
models.separateBecause: Frequency-specific results differ from a simple product rating
models.mergeOrDefer: Defer simulation and detailed taxonomy until a specialist workflow and corpus justify them

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Frequency-specific results differ from a simple product rating

priority.rationale: Possible specialist value but no current acoustic scenario and insufficient boundary conditions; low priority refers only to initial scope.

domains.name: Flexible evidence
domains.meaning: Preserve source detail and explain how curated values were chosen

models.name: Model evidence issues
models.question: Which missing or conflicting fields block this workflow?
models.decision: Prioritize data repair for a decision
models.grain: One evidence issue affecting a subject field and workflow in a snapshot
models.separateBecause: Missing fields have different consequences in different workflows
models.mergeOrDefer: Do not rank every optional missing field as an equal defect

existingContract.incrementalGain: Existing-contract fit still needs explicit review; Missing fields have different consequences in different workflows

scenarioSupport.supports: Incomplete inputs must remain visible rather than produce a pass.
scenarioSupport.doesNotEstablish: A comprehensive model-quality rule set or root-cause diagnosis.

priority.rationale: Unknown audit and handover cases justify actionable gaps; assignment and resolution histories require collaboration data.
